test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order forming a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. My mother, Vimala Kulkarni, told me similar words when I got married.

B. They were usually like: ‘You must adjust to your new house and in-laws, try to learn how they eat and cook their food, go out of your way to be friendly and helpful to everybody,’ etc.

C. When I was young, before a girl got married, her mother would give her some words of advice.

D. But along with this, she said something which helped me immensely in later life.
solution:
The correct answer is "**CBAD".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sentence C: - This is a general statement introducing the idea of advice given by mothers before marriage. It serves as a natural opening sentence.
 
• Sentence B: - This elaborates on what kind of advice mothers would give, logically following Sentence C.

 
 
• Sentence A: - This transitions to the author’s personal experience, following the general description in C and B.
 
• Sentence D: - This reflects on the impact of the advice and serves as a conclusion.

Hence, the **correct answer **is option 2. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **​__****BDAC (Incorrect)**: Starts with B, but there is no context given for the advice. Sentence C should introduce the idea before B elaborates on it.
 
• **CDBA (Incorrect):** After introducing the idea (C), it jumps to D, which reflects on something not yet discussed. The transition from C to D feels abrupt, breaking coherence.
 
• **ACBD (Incorrect):** Starts with A, which discusses the author’s mother directly. However, the context for her advice (given in C and B) is missing, making the start feel disjointed.
